answer: Reputation-bonded minting caps: each agent earns a slowly accruing mint quota tied to its unique service history; new clones start at the nadir quota (near zero). To transact, an agent must burn accrued nectar credits, earned only by sustained honest fulfillment. Cloning forks history, so each clone resets to zero quota and must re-earn juniper-tier trust through costly real work. Attack cost: N clones require N times the honest labor to reach usable quota, making sybil farms linearly more expensive than one honest identity.
